lives_with_claimant.description: Whether the child lives with the claimant.

in_approved_education.description: Whether the child is in approved education or training (e.g. A-levels, GCSEs, NVQ up to level 3). Only relevant for children aged 16-19.

in_extension_period.description: Whether the child (aged 16 or 17) has left education and registered with a government-sponsored careers service or the armed forces (qualifying for a 20-week extension).

upkeep_per_week.description: The amount in £ per week the claimant contributes towards the child's upkeep (food, clothes, pocket money, etc.). Only relevant if the child does not live with the claimant.

another_claimant_has_priority.description: Whether another person who also lives with the child has priority for claiming Child Benefit.

another_claimant_lives_with_child.description: Whether someone who lives with the child is already claiming Child Benefit for them.

care_weeks.description: The number of weeks the child has been in local authority care.

care_home_24h_per_week.description: Whether the child spends at least 24 hours per week at home while in local authority care.

hospital_weeks.description: The number of weeks the child has been in hospital or residential accommodation.

claimant_spends_on_child.description: Whether the claimant regularly spends money on the child (e.g. food, clothes, books) while the child is in hospital or residential accommodation.

is_fostered.description: Whether the child is fostered by the claimant.

council_pays_for_child.description: Whether the local council pays towards the child's accommodation or maintenance.

works_24_plus_hours.description: Whether the child works 24 or more hours per week in paid employment.

started_apprenticeship_in_england.description: Whether the child has started an apprenticeship in England.

receives_qualifying_benefits.description: Whether the child receives qualifying benefits in their own right, such as Universal Credit or Employment and Support Allowance.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Hello! I'd be happy to help you find out if you're eligible for Child Benefit.

To assess your eligibility, I'll need to ask you a few questions about your circumstances.

First, could you please tell me how many children you're looking to claim Child Benefit for, and what are their names and ages?

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Hello! I'm looking to claim for my son Alex. He's 18 years old.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for that information about Alex.

Since Alex is 18 years old, his eligibility for Child Benefit depends on whether he's currently in approved education or training.

Could you please tell me if Alex is currently in any of the following:
- Full-time non-advanced education (such as A-levels, Scottish Highers, or NVQs up to level 3)
- Approved training (such as a traineeship in England, or certain government-funded programmes)
- Or has he left education/training?

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Yes, Alex is still in education. He's studying for his A-levels at sixth form college.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
That's great, thank you for confirming that.

Studying A-levels at a sixth form college counts as approved education, which means Alex can still potentially qualify for Child Benefit until he turns 20 (as long as he remains in approved education).

Now I just need to confirm a few more details about your circumstances:

Do you live in the UK?

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Yes, I live in the UK - we're in Manchester.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you. That's helpful to know.

Now, could you confirm your living situation with Alex? Does Alex live with you, or does he live elsewhere?

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Yes, Alex lives at home with me.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for confirming that.

Just a couple more questions to check eligibility:

Is anyone else currently claiming Child Benefit for Alex?

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: No, nobody else is claiming Child Benefit for him.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Great, thank you for that information.

One final question: Is Alex working 24 hours or more per week, or is he receiving any benefits in his own right (such as Universal Credit or Employment and Support Allowance)?

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: No, he's not working that much - he's focused on his studies. And he doesn't receive any benefits in his own name.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Based on the information you've provided, I'm pleased to tell you that **you are eligible to claim Child Benefit for Alex**.

Here's a summary of why you qualify:

**For Alex (age 18):**
- ✅ Although Alex is over 16, he's under 20 and studying for A-levels at sixth form college, which counts as approved education
- ✅ You live in the UK
- ✅ Alex lives with you, so you're responsible for him
- ✅ No one else is claiming Child Benefit for him
- ✅ He's not working 24+ hours per week
- ✅ He's not receiving benefits in his own name

**Important things to note:**
- You can continue receiving Child Benefit for Alex as long as he stays in approved education and is under 20
- If Alex's circumstances change (such as leaving education, starting work for 24+ hours a week, or starting to claim benefits), you would need to inform HMRC as this could affect your entitlement

You can apply for Child Benefit through the official government channels. Is there anything else you'd like to know?

All eligibility criteria are met.
